                                                                    instance segmentation are learned simultaneously with a
                                                                    shared backbone. While highly effective, they depend on a
                                                                    large amount of instance and semantic annotations for fully
                                                                    supervised training. In this work, we seek to learn both se-
                                                                    mantic and instance-aware representations directly from un-
                                                                    labeled point clouds for enhancing performance on diverse
                                                                    segmentation tasks.

3. Method                                                        Offset Distribution Regularization (ODR) Regressing

approach. We first introduce the overall teacher–student         tions [7]. Therefore, directly introducing offset learning
architecture, which employs a prototype-based self-              into the self-supervised stage risks unstable optimization.
distillation mechanism as the semantic branch for learning       To mitigate this issue, we introduce Offset Distribution Reg-
category-level understanding. We then describe the offset        ularization (ODR), which constrains the predicted offsets to
branch, where the model learns to reason about geometric         match statistically grounded distributions observed in real
relationships among points. Finally, we present two com-         scenes. Each offset vector O ∈ R3 can be decomposed into
plementary regularization strategies that stabilize training     two components: (1) the magnitude, which measures the
and strengthen the geometric reasoning capability essential      distance to the instance centroid, and (2) the direction, a unit
for offset-based instance-aware learning.                        vector pointing toward that centroid. From our analysis of

Figure 3. Overview of PointINS: A point cloud is augmented to two independent views and they are randomly masked. The teacher
processes the full input and the student receives only visible points. Both networks share the same architecture. In the semantic branch,
features are computed similarity with prototypes Q. A KL-divergence loss Lsem is then applied for distillation. In the offset branch, an
offset head maps features into 3D offset vectors. Teacher offsets are first regularized by ODR to align with empirically observed geometric
priors. Next, segments obtained from K-means-clustering are used to extract pseudo-instance masks. Those masks help to enhance instance
awareness by regularizing local coherence of points. Finally, an offset loss Loff is computed as the second distillation.

Figure 6. Visualization of predicted centroids ci = xi +Oi (no explicit regularization) from models pre-trained under four configurations.
(a) Without regularization, the centroids are scattered irregularly across the scenes. (b) With ODR only, the centroids are aligned more
closely with the scene structure but they are not grouped (lack of local coherence). (c) With SCR only, the centroids are partially grouped
but spatially scattered. (d) With ODR and SCR, the centroids become tightly concentrated around instances.

also explore applying ODR on the student side, where the
regularization directly influences gradient updates in the                                      In this work, we introduce PointINS, a novel self-supervised
student backbone. This configuration again results in de-                                       learning framework that enables point cloud encoders to
graded performance, likely due to conflicting gradients and                                     jointly learn semantic invariance and instance-aware geo-
unstable optimization. In contrast, regularizing the teacher                                    metric reasoning without labels. By introducing two com-
outputs provides a stable and structured supervisory signal,                                    plementary regularization strategies applied to the geomet-
allowing the student to adapt smoothly without disrupting                                       ric learning, our method prevents model collapse while en-
representation learning [7, 29, 36].                                                            riching feature representations with geometric priors and
                                                                                                enforcing local coherence. PointINS achieves state-of-

our framework, we expand the pre-training pool by aggre-

                                                                                                portant step toward scalable 3D foundation models capable
ScanNet [12], S3DIS [21], and Structured3D [45], yield-

                           ĉi ← xi + Õi                       Table 13. Results of unsupervised instance segmentation on Scan-
                                                                Net.
 2: Global feature grouping:

            {S1 , . . . , SK } ← KMeans(F; K, iter)

 3: Local spatial clustering per segment:
    For each segment Sk :
    (a) Compute k nearest neighbors for each point i ∈ Sk
    using Euclidean distance in centroid space:

                     N (i) = kNN(ĉi , knn )

    Retain edges only if distance is below threshold:

               j ∈ N (i)     iff       ∥ĉi − ĉj ∥2 < τd

    (b) Extract connected components using Breadth-First
    Search (BFS):
                       Ik = BFS(N )
    (c) Remove small components (noise filtering):

               Ik ← {Ik,j ∈ Ik | |Ik,j | ≥ τmin }

 4: Compute refined centroids:

                                   1        X
                       c̄k,j =                      ĉi
                                 |Ik,j |
                                           i∈Ik,j

 5: Generate new offset targets:

                  Oi∗ = c̄k,j − xi ,         ∀i ∈ Ik,j

 6: return {Oi∗ }N

head, we directly use the offsets predicted by the pretrained
model and perform BFS-based clustering on the offset-
shifted centroids to generate instance proposals. The re-
sulting clusters are matched to ground-truth instances via
Hungarian assignment for evaluation. As shown in Tab. 13,
PointINS substantially outperforms classical unsupervised
baselines such as HDBSCAN [6] and Felzenszwalb clus-
